title: Optio — All your agent work. One place to run it.
excerpt: Coding agents, scheduled jobs, event automations, and interactive sessions. Your cluster, your machines, and native apps in your pocket.
content_html:
Open-source agent orchestration

Your agents.
Your infrastructure.
One workspace.

Turn a prompt into a pull request. Put a workflow on a schedule. Pick up a session from your phone.

Optio runs coding agents and automations on your Kubernetes cluster or your own machines—with one place to follow the work.

jonwiggins/optio · Self-hosted · MIT licensed · Web, iOS & Android

Your agent. Your choice.

Claude CodeOpenAI CodexGitHub CopilotGoogle GeminiCursorOpenCodeOpenClaw

Built around the work

From the first prompt
to the next step.

Optio handles the environment, triggers, and follow-through around your agents. You decide what to delegate and when to step in.

01DEVELOPMENT

From issue to pull request.

Give an agent a repository and a bounded change. It works in a git worktree, opens a PR, and can resume with review feedback while Optio follows CI and merge status.

Issue → Worktree → Agent → PR → Review

Explore repo workflows

02AUTOMATION

Make the routine run itself.

Schedule dependency updates, prepare a daily briefing, or investigate an incident. Turn event payloads into prompt parameters and keep the logs and outcome of every run.

Schedule or event → Run → Result

Explore triggers & integrations

03COLLABORATION

Keep a specialist on hand.

Give persistent agents a name, instructions, and an inbox. They work in turns, wake on messages or triggers, and can coordinate with other agents in your workspace.

Message → Agent turn → Reply → Wait

Explore persistent agents

work in motion.

One feed for tasks, recurring workflows, sessions, and persistent agents. Open the conversation, follow a run, or return to the terminal.

A home for every kind of work.

Native iOS and Android apps keep the same workspace within reach. Check the queue, reply to an agent, open a terminal, or start new work.

  • Conversations and terminals on your phone
  • Widgets and notifications for work that needs you
  • iOS Live Activities and Apple Watch Smart Stack

Native apps built from source. Screens show fictional example work.

A closer look

The details stay connected.

From the event that started a run to the conversation that moves it forward. Open a screen to explore it at full size.

What do I need to run Optio?

A Kubernetes cluster, PostgreSQL, and Redis run the control plane. The local setup script deploys these with Docker Desktop. Bring credentials for the agent runtime you want to use; Optio Local can also connect your own machines for execution.

Can I use my existing agent and model?

Choose a runtime for each piece of work, with the models and authentication methods that runtime supports. On a paired machine, Optio Local uses the CLI configuration and login already installed there. You can also run a shell command without an LLM.

Does every workflow need a repository?

No. Repository work can produce pull requests, while standalone work can query connected tools, generate reports, or run commands. Interactive sessions and persistent agents support other ways of working. The Work form offers the combinations that fit.

How much control do I have over agents?

Choose the connections, tools, and skills available to pod work. Configure code review, draft PRs, and automatic resume limits. Per-work settings can tighten a repository’s PR policies. Use organization or private ownership and workspace roles to manage access.

Is Optio free, and where does my data go?

Optio is open source under the MIT license. You operate its infrastructure and store its state. Your chosen agents still communicate with their model providers and connected services; those services and your infrastructure may have their own costs.

starts here.

Deploy locally with Docker Desktop and Kubernetes, connect an agent, and give it something useful to do.

git clone https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio.git
cd optio
./scripts/setup-local.sh

Requires Docker Desktop with Kubernetes, Node.js 22+, pnpm 10+, Helm 3+, and kubectl.
